title: Cicada 3301: The Internet's Hardest Puzzle Was Never Solved
creator: Nadia Okafor
description:
In 2012 an anonymous group posted a puzzle on 4chan. Thousands tried to solve it. Almost nobody got to the end, and nobody knows who was behind it.

sentences.t: On January fourth, 2012, someone posted a single image to an anonymous imageboard.
It was white text on a black background, and it said, hello, we are looking for highly intelligent individuals.
To find them, we have devised a test.
There's a message hidden in this image, find it, and it will lead you on the road to finding us.
It was signed with just a number, 3301.
And at first, most people assumed it was a troll, or maybe an alternate reality game for some movie.
But a few people opened the image in a text editor, and sure enough, buried in the file data was a hidden message.
That message was encoded with a Caesar cipher, which led to a web address, which led to a picture of a duck that said, woops, just decoys this way.
And honestly, that duck is when the internet decided to take this seriously.
Over the next few weeks the puzzle sent people through book ciphers, steganography, Mayan numerals, and a phone number in Texas that played a recorded message.
Thousands of people were working on it by then, and nobody had any idea how deep it went.
Ever wondered how much of your personal info is just sitting out there right now for anyone to buy?
Your home address, your phone number, your relatives' names, even roughly how much your house is worth.

So, real-world locations.
A few days into the puzzle, the clues stopped being online at all.
Solvers found GPS coordinates that pointed to telephone poles in fourteen cities across five countries, from Warsaw to Seattle to Sydney.
And on each pole was a printed poster with a cicada on it and a QR code.
People in chat rooms were literally coordinating, like, does anyone live near Miami, can someone go check a pole.
The QR codes led to a site on the Tor network, and that site only opened for a few hours before it said it had found what it was looking for.
A handful of people supposedly got private emails after that, and then they went quiet.
Some of them have since said they were asked to join a group interested in privacy and encryption, and that was it.
No reveal, no recruitment for a spy agency, no answer.
The puzzle came back in 2013 and again in 2014, each one harder than the last, and then in 2017 a message appeared warning people that anything not signed with their key was fake.
Since then, nothing.
So who was it?
My honest take is that it was a small group of very smart cryptography nerds who wanted to find other cryptography nerds.
Tell me your theory in the comments, I read all of them.
